name: prettier
why: The formatter decides the shape of the prose files, and it is fetched at run time with no package manifest and no lockfile in the tree. That is a cost the formatting gate took deliberately, and this is where it is paid for: the version is here, the workflow reads it, and the run below says when the registry has moved past it. The registry publishes no digest a caller can hold the download to, so this pin has no checksum and the gap is the field being empty rather than a value nobody checked.

name: zizmor
why: The workflow audit is the check that reads the workflow files, so a version of it that stops matching the syntax it audits is the one drift nothing else in this tree would notice. It is installed from a prebuilt wheel at run time, and the resolver compares against what the index publishes rather than against the wheel, so what this watches is the release and not the bytes.

name: semgrep
why: The static analysis over the generator source is the check that decides the shapes this project has ruled out, and the rules are written against the patterns one release of the engine understands. A release that changes how a pattern is matched turns a rule that refuses something into a rule that refuses nothing, and the run stays green either way, so this is the drift with no other witness. It is installed from a prebuilt wheel at run time and the resolver compares against what the index publishes rather than against the wheel, so what this watches is the release and not the bytes.

name: library/golang
why: The container builds the site from this image, and the digest is what makes that build the same one twice. It is repeated rather than read because a FROM instruction takes no indirection, so the reference is derived from the fields here and the file is refused when it carries a different one. What the run compares is the digest the tag resolves to today, because a tag rebuilt under the same name is exactly the drift a version string would not see.
